result.text: The paper addresses robust test-time adaptation under distribution shift by detecting when a classifier’s predictive uncertainty (entropy) departs from the source distribution and adapting only when needed. The key insight is to monitor the stream of unlabeled test entropies with a betting-martingale-style detector and to adapt the model so that the test-time entropy distribution is driven to match the source entropy distribution, rather than simply minimizing entropy as in conventional self-training. Methodologically, the authors combine online betting/martingale change-detection with an adaptation update derived from a connection to optimal transport to construct a self-supervised loss that dynamically triggers and guides parameter updates; experiments show this improves accuracy under shifts while preserving calibration and performance when no shift occurs.

Its key insight is a theoretical loss upper bound relating pre- and post-eviction attention outputs, which reveals that heads have different sensitivities and thus should receive different eviction budgets to minimize output distortion. result.text: We propose an active data-collection scheme that jointly designs multi-view co-visibility and unlabeled sparse intervention codes to certify identifiability of object-wise causal latents with minimal episodes. Online, we maintain an estimated co-visibility hypergraph and choose next camera poses and action primitives by greedily maximizing a submodular surrogate of the identifiability margin—tightening the RIP-like compressed-sensing condition over slots and ensuring pairwise-connected co-visibility—while using group-testing-style randomized intervention patterns that are unlabeled but decodable from pre/post signatures. Theoretically, under an object-compositional generative model with partial observability, O(s log n) episodes with these view–intervention designs suffice with high probability to recover slots and interventional effects up to permutation; practically, we instantiate this with a slot-contrastive encoder that estimates per-episode Fisher information to drive selection. This turns passive guarantees into an adaptive procedure that reduces sample and camera budgets while preserving identifiability under occlusion.

result.text: The paper addresses online uncertainty quantification where data distributions can shift arbitrarily over time, aiming to produce prediction sets with valid coverage and low regret even within changing environments. Its key insight is that standard regret minimization is insufficient for nonstationary settings, so one should target strongly adaptive regret — the worst-case regret over all intervals of a given length — to ensure good performance not just overall but on every subinterval. The authors develop online conformal prediction procedures that incorporate strongly adaptive online learning algorithms to minimize this interval-wise regret while maintaining approximate coverage guarantees, proving near-optimal strongly adaptive regret simultaneously across all interval lengths. Empirically, these methods yield more reliable coverage and smaller prediction sets than prior approaches on time-series forecasting and image classification tasks with distribution shift.

result.text: The paper addresses the persistent problem of object hallucinations in large vision-language models (LVLMs), where models generate visually inconsistent or non-existent object references. The key insight is that hallucinations can be reduced by jointly leveraging fine-grained local grounding to correct tokens as they are produced and a global search strategy to favor grounded hypotheses during sequence decoding. HALC implements this by adding an auto-focal grounding mechanism that dynamically assesses and rectifies token-level visual alignment, combined with a specialized beam-search decoding that re-ranks beams based on grounding consistency, and it operates as a plug-and-play decoding module requiring no additional training. Experimental results across four benchmarks show that this dual local–global approach lowers object hallucinations while maintaining generation quality, outperforming prior methods.

result.text: The paper tackles the KV-cache memory bottleneck in LLM decoding, where storing key-value pairs for all previous tokens limits deployment and existing pruning/eviction schemes hurt tasks needing long-range recall. The key insight is that adding a tiny, constant-sized recurrent cache that synthesizes and preserves summarized recurrence can complement eviction-based caches so that no token is truly unrecoverable, allowing the model to query approximate historical information without storing all KV pairs. The method, called LESS, integrates a nearly-free fixed-size recurrent cache with standard eviction or pruning strategies: during decoding LESS maintains and updates a compact summary representation of past states while evicted full KV entries remain removable, enabling the decoder to reconstruct or approximate older context when needed. Experiments show LESS substantially narrows (and sometimes closes) the performance gap with full caching across diverse tasks while drastically reducing memory use.

args.text: We propose Federated Basis-Routed LoRA (FeBRuS): a server learns a global per-layer low-rank basis plus a few cluster-specific sub-bases from federated client updates, while each client personalizes via sparse, nonnegative coefficients and a tiny on-device router over these bases. Only aggregated basis gradients are shared with secure aggregation; client-specific coefficients remain local, yet at inference a client can attach its compact coefficient vector or cluster tag so the server applies its adapter in a batched pass using FLoRA-style per-example tagging. This yields multi-tenant throughput with privacy and continual cross-client transfer as the shared basis improves, and supports cold-start by Arrow-style zero-shot routing onto the nearest basis mix. The design unifies federated heterogeneous-rank tuning, shared-basis compression, and batchable execution into a practical private serving pipeline.

result.text: ShadowTool is an emulator-guided, cost- and risk-aware toolchain selector for LLM agents: it prunes and ranks candidate multi-step tool plans before any expensive real invocations. It combines tree-of-plans generation with an LM-based tool emulator and safety evaluator to cheaply simulate alternatives, while a contextual reliability prior fit on real tool traces and fine-grained progress signals estimates per-step success and value-of-information. Evaluated on tool-selection benchmarks and end-to-end real-tool tasks, ShadowTool aims to cut real tool calls and catastrophic failures without sacrificing accuracy.

result.text: The paper addresses the neglected problem of relationship hallucinations in large vision-language models (LVLMs), where models invent or misattribute relationships between objects despite object detection being largely solvable. Its key insight is that relationship hallucinations arise from specific co-occurrence biases—relationship-relationship, subject-relationship, and relationship-object—and from long-tail distributions in visual instruction tuning data that push models to over-rely on language priors rather than visual evidence. To quantify and analyze this, the authors introduce R-Bench, a benchmark comprising image-level and instance-level questions designed to probe existence and local comprehension of visual relationships, and use it to show that current LVLMs often ignore visual content, depend on commonsense LLM knowledge, and fail at contextual spatial reasoning. Their empirical analysis highlights dataset bias and model tendencies as primary drivers of relationship hallucination and points to the need for targeted data and evaluation to improve relational visual reasoning.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of ballooning Key-Value (KV) cache size and the resulting memory/time costs when LLMs process very long contexts. The key insight is that individual attention heads consistently attend to a small set of prompt positions and that this head-specific attention pattern can be predicted from a short “observation” window at the end of the prompt. SnapKV leverages this by clustering and selecting the important KV positions per head (without finetuning) and only storing those compressed KV entries during generation, yielding similar accuracy while keeping decoding latency stable and dramatically reducing memory use. Empirically, SnapKV speeds decoding ~3.6×, improves memory efficiency ~8.2× on 16K inputs, scales to ~380K tokens on a single A100 with negligible accuracy loss, and maintains baseline performance across 16 long-context datasets.

result.text: We propose Federated Basis-Routed LoRA (FeBRuS): a server learns a global per-layer low-rank basis plus a few cluster-specific sub-bases from federated client updates, while each client personalizes via sparse, nonnegative coefficients and a tiny on-device router over these bases. The design unifies federated heterogeneous-rank tuning, shared-basis compression, and batchable execution into a practical private serving pipeline.

result.text: We propose an active data-collection scheme that jointly designs multi-view co-visibility and unlabeled sparse intervention codes to certify identifiability of object-wise causal latents with minimal episodes. Online, we maintain an estimated co-visibility hypergraph and choose next camera poses and action primitives by greedily maximizing a submodular surrogate of the identifiability margin—tightening the RIP-like compressed-sensing condition over slots and ensuring pairwise-connected co-visibility—while using group-testing-style randomized intervention patterns that are unlabeled but decodable from pre/post signatures. Theoretically, under an object-compositional generative model with partial observability, O(s log n) episodes with these view–intervention designs suffice with high probability to recover slots and interventional effects up to permutation; practically, we instantiate this with a slot-contrastive encoder that estimates per-episode Fisher information to drive selection. This turns passive guarantees into an adaptive procedure that reduces sample and camera budgets while preserving identifiability under occlusion.

result.text: The paper tackles the failure of existing test-time adaptation (TTA) methods when unlabeled test data arrive as temporally correlated, non-i.i.d. streams (e.g., in autonomous driving) rather than the commonly assumed i.i.d. setting. The key insight is that adapting batch statistics and sample selection to account for out-of-distribution instances and class imbalance in the incoming stream can restore reliable adaptation under temporal correlation. Concretely, the authors introduce Instance-Aware Batch Normalization (IABN) to correct normalization for OOD or shifted samples and Prediction-balanced Reservoir Sampling (PBRS) to maintain a class-balanced reservoir that simulates an i.i.d. stream from a non-i.i.d. sequence, and they integrate these with TTA training updates. Experiments on several datasets, including real-world non-i.i.d. streams, show the method substantially improves robustness over prior TTA approaches while matching their performance in i.i.d. scenarios.

We translate natural-language specs to LTL and align VLM and visual inputs to the generative latent space (mitigating the modality gap), then learn atomic-proposition classifiers with conformal calibration to output prediction sets over truth values and compile them into probabilistic differentiable automata that propagate lower/upper satisfaction bounds along latent rollouts. Policies are trained to maximize an eventual-discounted lower bound on satisfaction probability while receiving intrinsic bonuses for shrinking monitor uncertainty, with an active data-collection loop that queries labels or privileged “restraining bolt” features only when conformal risk exceeds a budget. This yields robust satisfaction under distribution shift, safer constraint enforcement, and improved generalization to unseen LTL tasks.

To realize this, the authors derive learning-theoretic guarantees for ATTA, propose a sample-entropy balancing strategy to avoid forgetting, and introduce SimATTA, a lightweight real-time sample-selection algorithm that integrates label queries into TTA. Empirical evaluations across benchmarks show that SimATTA substantially outperforms standard TTA methods and approaches the performance of heavier active domain adaptation approaches while remaining efficient.

args.text: Tree-Conformal Planning supplies plan-level, branch-aware conformal risk certificates for LLM tool agents by replacing per-step calibration and union bounds with structured, path-wise nonconformity and joint-valid prediction sets over entire execution paths. Concretely, it learns nonconformity on abstracted toolkit-and-prompt paths and solves a joint-coverage parameterization (inspired by multi-step time-series conformal) to pick primary and contingency branches that minimize a dual-informed plan-set length while satisfying a global alpha budget. Online, it maintains long-run coverage with adaptive conformal updates; when coverage martingales flag shift, it triggers safe micro-adaptations (label-prior recalibration or covariate-robust entropy minimization) and intra-toolkit swaps, rolling back updates that fail to restore target coverage on a reservoir. Compared to risk-budget allocators and stepwise conformal gates, this yields tighter plan-level guarantees and fewer unnecessary probes/branchings at the same tail risk.

result.text: We propose an identifiability algebra for object-centric multi-view causal representation learning under occlusion: when each view reveals only a subset of objects, the co-visibility hypergraph across views and scenes can guarantee recovery of object-wise causal latents up to per-slot reparameterizations. Concretely, under a compositional-and-irreducible object generative process and smooth view-dependent mixing, identifiability holds if (i) the co-visibility hypergraph is pairwise-connected (every slot chain-co-occurs across some sequence of view subsets) and (ii) each slot experiences at least one sparse, slot-targeted perturbation across the dataset—or, alternatively, instance-dependent sparsity of slot visibility provides sufficient support variation. We instantiate this with a contrastive, multi-view slot encoder that enforces cycle-consistent slot matching on the co-visibility graph and a causal-loss that anchors which slot changed under interventions, yielding stronger guarantees and fewer required perturbations than monolithic encoders. This unifies multi-view partial-observability, object-centric structure, and sparsity/interventions into a single theoretical and algorithmic framework.

result.text: The paper addresses instability and inefficiency when applying Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) in privacy-preserving federated learning, where data heterogeneity, multi-step local updates, and differentially private (DP) noise amplify training variance and make hyper-parameter tuning fragile. The key insight is that the instability stems from discordant joint optimization of the two low-rank matrices on clients followed by separate aggregation at the server, so freezing one of the paired matrices (keeping a randomly initialized non-zero matrix fixed) while only fine-tuning the zero-initialized counterpart reduces mismatch and sensitivity. The proposed method, Federated Freeze A LoRA (FFA-LoRA), fixes the non-zero LoRA matrices and transmits/aggregates only the trainable zero-initialized matrices, which halves communication cost, mitigates DP noise amplification, and yields more consistent performance and computational efficiency than vanilla LoRA across federated tasks.

args.text: We propose AC-TTA: Active-Conformal Test-Time Adaptation for non-i.i.d. streams that queries labels only when uncertainty certificates cannot be restored by safe unsupervised updates. AC-TTA maintains online conformal coverage using entropy-based nonconformity and a betting-martingale shift detector to trigger a small number of trust-region micro-updates on a PBRS/IABN-buffered batch; if coverage and the nonconformity distribution fail to recover, it allocates a query from a tight label budget chosen by maximal prediction-set size or margin. Queried labels recalibrate conformal scores, anchor the model via lightweight supervised corrections, and populate a small replay buffer to prevent forgetting, while routine operation remains fully unsupervised. This hybrid controller targets minimal query rates with guaranteed coverage recovery and improved robustness on temporally correlated streams over purely unsupervised or always-on ATTA baselines.

result.text: Tree-Conformal Planning supplies plan-level, branch-aware conformal risk certificates for LLM tool agents by replacing per-step calibration and union bounds with structured, path-wise nonconformity and joint-valid prediction sets over entire execution paths. Concretely, it learns nonconformity on abstracted toolkit-and-prompt paths and solves a joint-coverage parameterization (inspired by multi-step time-series conformal) to pick primary and contingency branches that minimize a dual-informed plan-set length while satisfying a global alpha budget. Online, it maintains long-run coverage with adaptive conformal updates; when coverage martingales flag shift, it triggers safe micro-adaptations (label-prior recalibration or covariate-robust entropy minimization) and intra-toolkit swaps, rolling back updates that fail to restore target coverage on a reservoir. Compared to risk-budget allocators and stepwise conformal gates, this yields tighter plan-level guarantees and fewer unnecessary probes/branchings at the same tail risk.

result.text: Query-Aware Retrieval and Cache Scheduling (QuARCS) is a RAG decoding scheme that jointly routes attention over retrieved-document caches and the model’s own KV cache pages at each token. Building on Sparse RAG’s per-document cache gating, QuARCS adds a query-conditioned pager like Quest to load only the top-K KV pages and uses ZipCache-style normalized attention proxies computed by a tiny draft step (run in PEARL-style overlap) to prefetch the next-step document caches most likely to be needed. A tiny recurrent summary cache (LESS) shadows both the conversation and each retrieved document, enabling aggressive eviction of rarely used caches while preserving recoverable long-range recall. This tight coupling of routing, prefetch, and speculative overlap reduces IO stalls and context distraction, targeting end-to-end speedups with equal-or-better grounding quality versus Speculative RAG.

result.text: We propose ULTRA: an uncertainty‑calibrated latent temporal reward monitor that compiles natural‑language or LTL task specifications into executable automata operating directly on a learned world‑model latent space, providing dense, cheap feedback during imagination. Concretely, we align language and vision to the generative latent space (GenRL‑style grounding while mitigating the modality gap) and learn a dictionary of atomic propositions as lightweight latent classifiers with NML‑style calibrated uncertainty; these are then compiled (à la spec‑to‑reward) into differentiable automata that run each latent rollout step. During imagination we use the automata outputs as shaped rewards plus an intrinsic bonus from classifier uncertainty, and augment training with counterfactual satisfaction rollouts and an eventual‑discounting objective to maximize long‑run satisfaction probability. Using an S4‑based world model yields long‑horizon credit assignment and efficient monitoring, promising promptable generalists that learn from language without external reward queries.

result.text: The paper addresses how to learn shared representations for multi-task reinforcement learning that capture both commonalities and task-specific differences while avoiding redundant or collapsed features. Its key insight is that enforcing orthogonality among expert-generated representations encourages diversity and a compact shared subspace that can be flexibly combined to represent different tasks. The proposed method, Mixture Of Orthogonal Experts (MOORE), builds a mixture-of-experts encoder whose expert outputs are orthogonalized via a Gram–Schmidt process to form a shared subspace, and a task-conditioned gating mechanism selects relevant combinations from that subspace to produce task-specific representations for policy learning. Evaluated on MiniGrid and MetaWorld, MOORE outperforms prior baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance on MetaWorld.

result.text: The paper tackles hallucinations in large vision-language models (LVLMs), where models generate incorrect or ungrounded text, without relying on costly extra data or doubling inference. Its key insight is that pretrained LVLMs can introspectively judge the importance of visual tokens conditioned on prior vision and text context, so selectively removing unimportant vision tokens early can amplify text-informed hallucination signals that reveal vision-text associations. The method, Self-Introspective Decoding (SID), uses a Context and Text-aware Token Selection (CT2S) strategy to prune unimportant vision tokens after early layers, computes amplified hallucination logits driven by the remaining vision-text association, and subtracts these from the original token logits during autoregressive decoding to suppress aimless visual hallucinations. Experiments show SID reduces hallucinations and improves text quality across metrics without extra knowledge sources and with minimal added computation.

result.text: Risk-Budgeted Contingency Trees (RBCT) allocate and enforce a global tail-risk budget across an LLM agent’s branched tool-execution plan. result.text: The paper tackles hallucination in large multimodal models—erroneous text output that is inconsistent with visual input—by proposing a decoding-time fix rather than retraining. The key insight is to use the model’s own detailed, self-generated descriptions of the image as contrastive references: comparing candidate continuations against those descriptions helps identify and suppress tokens that deviate from the actual visual content. The method, COuntering DEscription Contrastive Decoding (CODE), computes token-level adjustments during decoding by dynamically reweighting next-token probabilities based on similarity to the self-generated description versus the primary prompt-conditioned distribution, thereby steering generation toward outputs aligned with the visual counterpart. CODE is a plug-in contrastive decoding strategy that requires no extra training and empirically reduces hallucinations and improves cross-modal consistency across multiple benchmarks.

Contrastive Utility-Guided Adaptive Routing (CUGAR): learn a gating policy that chooses both which experts and how many to activate per token by directly optimizing a compute-regularized utility estimated from contrastive routing signals. During training, stochastically sample additional candidate experts for a token and use a self-contrast improvement metric (e.g., delta in token log-prob between weak vs. strong activations) as a per-token reward; a lightweight policy head over gating logits is trained with policy gradients to allocate extra experts only when marginal gain exceeds a learned compute penalty calibrated by routed scaling-law fits. result.text: The paper addresses the inefficiency and instability of depth-adaptive Transformers that use learned halting units to decide per-token computation depth, which can be poorly supervised and yield suboptimal stopping decisions. The key insight is that required depths can be estimated in advance by directly measuring token "hardness" rather than relying on an online halting unit, enabling faster and more stable depth adaptation. The authors propose two explicit hardness estimators—one based on mutual information (MI) between token representations and labels, and another based on reconstruction loss from an auxiliary decoder—and use these estimates to assign per-token depths so the Transformer only computes the needed layers. Experiments on 24 text-classification datasets show that these pre-estimation methods yield up to 7x speedups over a vanilla Transformer while maintaining accuracy and improving efficiency and robustness relative to prior depth-adaptive approaches.

args.text: Risk-Adaptive Alpha Scheduling (RAAS) augments conformal tool planning with a learned, state- and prefix-aware schedule for an agent’s global coverage budget across plan branches. RAAS optimizes per-prefix alpha allocations and contingency set sizes on an abstract toolkit graph to minimize expected time/cost under a joint plan-level coverage constraint, combining path-wise conformal sets with an online adaptive wrapper to preserve long-run validity under shift. The scheduler is trained end-to-end with a robust policy-gradient surrogate that treats emulator-predicted step outcomes as a nominal kernel and guards against low-rank worst-case perturbations, while a dynamic risk-level predictor adjusts alpha online from early anomaly signals. At runtime, RAAS interoperates with toolkit-level substitution and conformal gates, reallocating remaining risk as branches succeed/fail and triggering safe micro-adaptations only when coverage martingales flag drift.

We propose Equivariance-Consistency Decoding (ECD), a training-free controller that suppresses hallucinations by requiring token-level visual evidence to transform predictably under small image symmetries. At each decoding step, we apply a handful of test-time transformations (e.g., jittered translations/rotations) and estimate a Lie-derivative-style sensitivity of each candidate object/attribute token’s grounding signal (cross-attention/CAM) to these generators; candidates whose evidence is non-equivariant receive adaptive logit penalties that integrate into HALC-style global re-ranking. ECD distinguishes genuine visual cues from language priors that fail to persist across views, reducing multi-object and relation hallucinations without extra data or fine-tuning.

result.text: We propose identifiable object-centric multi-view causal representation learning under occlusion and unlabeled sparse interventions. Each view observes a nonlinear mixture of a subset of objects, and episodes provide pre/post pairs where a single object property is perturbed but the object identity and affected view(s) are unknown. By combining object-level compositional irreducibility with the multi-view identifiability algebra, we show the object latents and cross-view correspondences are uniquely recoverable (up to permutation) when each object is visible in at least two views across episodes and receives occasional perturbations; we instantiate this with contrastively aligned slot encoders whose slots predict which views registered the change. This reduces supervision relative to labeled interventions and improves sample efficiency under heavy occlusion versus monolithic encoders.

This fuses uncertainty-aware conditioning, MoE scaling, and diversity-preserving regularization to improve zero-shot generalization on procedurally diverse benchmarks.

result.text: We propose Equivariance-Consistency Decoding (ECD), a training-free controller that suppresses hallucinations by requiring token-level visual evidence to transform predictably under small image symmetries. At each decoding step, we apply a handful of test-time transformations (e.g., jittered translations/rotations) and estimate a Lie-derivative-style sensitivity of each candidate object/attribute token’s grounding signal (cross-attention/CAM) to these generators; candidates whose evidence is non-equivariant receive adaptive logit penalties that integrate into HALC-style global re-ranking. ECD distinguishes genuine visual cues from language priors that fail to persist across views, reducing multi-object and relation hallucinations without extra data or fine-tuning.

result.text: We propose identifiable object-centric multi-view causal representation learning under occlusion and unlabeled sparse interventions. Each view observes a nonlinear mixture of a subset of objects, and episodes provide pre/post pairs where a single object property is perturbed but the object identity and affected view(s) are unknown. By combining object-level compositional irreducibility with the multi-view identifiability algebra, we show the object latents and cross-view correspondences are uniquely recoverable (up to permutation) when each object is visible in at least two views across episodes and receives occasional perturbations; we instantiate this with contrastively aligned slot encoders whose slots predict which views registered the change. This reduces supervision relative to labeled interventions and improves sample efficiency under heavy occlusion versus monolithic encoders.

result.text: Uncertainty-routed specialist distillation for scalable RL generalization: start by training a broad generalist, then use ensemble-based epistemic inference to cluster environment variations into latent regimes and spawn specialists initialized from the generalist for each regime. result.text: The paper tackles the vulnerability of test-time adaptation (TTA) methods to noisy, unexpected samples in unlabeled test streams—scenarios like unseen objects or corrupted inputs where existing TTA algorithms can be misled by blindly adapting to every incoming example. The key insight is that robustness requires screening out harmful inputs and stabilizing parameter updates: selectively adapting on high-confidence, class-uniform samples reduces the influence of outliers, while minimizing an entropy-sharpness objective guards parameters against destabilizing large gradients. The proposed method, SoTTA, implements input-wise robustness via high-confidence uniform-class sampling to filter test data and parameter-wise robustness through entropy-sharpness minimization during adaptation, and experiments on standard TTA benchmarks with various noisy conditions show SoTTA outperforms prior methods under noise while matching their accuracy on clean streams.

result.text: We propose Conformal-Constrained Test-Time Adaptation (CoCo-TTA), an online wrapper that couples entropy-minimization with an explicit calibration-control constraint to maintain long-run coverage while improving accuracy under shift. A streaming conformal monitor tracks nonconformity quantiles on a small reservoir and updates a dual variable that jointly scales the adaptation step size and a trust-region penalty; updates are triggered by a martingale shift detector and applied only to low-entropy, diverse samples. The resulting primal–dual procedure minimizes marginal-entropy (or pseudo-label loss) subject to matching a target coverage/calibration profile, with rollback if reservoir coverage or an entropy–sharpness surrogate degrades. CoCo-TTA yields safe, selective adaptation that boosts accuracy under shift while preserving near-nominal calibration in the no-shift regime.

result.text: The paper tackles the latency and compute blowup in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) caused by linearly increasing input length as more documents are retrieved. Its key insight is that most retrieved documents are irrelevant to each generation step, so encoding them in parallel and then sparsely selecting a small subset to attend to during autoregressive decoding can preserve quality while cutting computation. The proposed Sparse RAG encodes all retrieved documents independently into caches, prompts the LLM with special control tokens to assess and choose highly relevant caches on the fly, and then decodes by attending only to those selected caches, thereby merging per-document relevance assessment and generation into a single process. Empirical results on short- and long-form tasks show this sparse mechanism reduces the number of documents loaded during decoding, accelerating inference and often improving generation by filtering out distracting context.

result.text: The paper addresses representation collapse in sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, where routing tokens to experts based on hidden representations causes tokens to cluster around expert centroids and reduces representation diversity. The key insight is that computing routing scores on a low-dimensional hypersphere mitigates this collapse by decoupling routing similarity from high-dimensional magnitude and promoting more uniform, stable token-expert assignments. Methodologically, the authors project token and expert representations onto a low-dimensional spherical embedding space and compute routing scores there, then evaluate the approach through extensive cross-lingual pretraining and downstream fine-tuning across seven multilingual benchmarks. Experiments and analyses show the spherical routing reduces collapse, yields more consistent routing behavior, and produces consistent performance gains over baseline MoE methods.

At inference, HaCARL routes new inputs to the nearest adapter mix and progressively increases rank only for persistently hard tokens/layers, yielding SLO-aware throughput gains while preserving accuracy across heterogeneous tenants.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of instructing goal-conditioned reinforcement learning agents to satisfy temporally extended tasks specified in Linear Temporal Logic (LTL), addressing poor generalization of prior methods that require extensive LTL-task training and are limited to regular-expression-like specifications. The key insight is that a simple goal-conditioned RL agent, when coupled with a principled translation from arbitrary LTL (including ω-regular) objectives into a sequence of goal-conditioning queries and internal automaton guidance, can be steered to satisfy complex temporal objectives without retraining on the LTL task distribution. The method constructs an automaton representation of the LTL formula and uses it to decompose the specification into temporally ordered subgoals, then queries the pre-trained goal-conditioned policy zero-shot to achieve those subgoals while tracking automaton progress, enabling satisfaction of broad classes of temporal specifications; experiments show this approach adapts to complex LTL tasks zero-shot and outperforms prior restricted techniques.

result.text: We propose physics-anchored identifiability for object-centric multi-view videos under occlusion by exploiting sparse contact impulses as unlabeled, slot-targeted interventions. When rigid-body interactions are s-sparse within short windows, masses/inertias are generic, and the time-augmented co-visibility graph is pairwise-connected, impulse–momentum consistency across views supplies change anchors that render object latents and cross-view correspondences identifiable up to slot permutation and per-slot reparameterizations. Algorithmically, we couple a contrastive multi-view slot encoder with a differentiable impulse–momentum layer that enforces conservation across candidate slot trajectories and uses impulsive residuals (optionally time-anchored by audio spikes) to localize which slots interacted. An active planner induces gentle taps or vibrations to excite informative contacts, selecting camera poses and excitation timings to close algebra-predicted identifiability gaps with fewer episodes than object or lighting perturbations.

result.text: The paper addresses how to construct effective curricula for reinforcement learning by formally interpolating between an easy auxiliary (source) task distribution and a hard target distribution to enable gradual learning. Its key insight is to view curriculum generation as an optimal transport problem and to produce a sequence of intermediate task distributions along a geodesic (Wasserstein barycenter) between source and target, using a task-dependent contextual distance so shifts are small and meaningful. The proposed method, GRADIENT, computes these Wasserstein-geodesic interpolations for nonparametric continuous or discrete context distributions and schedules training across the resulting stages; the authors also provide theoretical conditions guaranteeing smooth transfer between adjacent stages and empirically demonstrate improved learning efficiency and final performance on locomotion and manipulation benchmarks.

Under compositional irreducibility and smooth view-dependent mixing, identifiability holds when the view-by-episode focus schedule induces a pairwise-connected co-visibility-with-sharpness graph and a RIP/expander-like code over depth-ordered slots; a differentiable optics layer models circle-of-confusion PSFs to align slots across focus states. We instantiate a planner that co-designs camera poses and focus/aperture sequences to maximize these identifiability metrics given coarse depth priors, and a slot-contrastive encoder with defocus-aware gating and cycle/anchor losses, achieving fewer episodes than lighting/object perturbations while remaining robust to heavy occlusions. result.text: Current query-aware KV paging reduces loads by scoring existing cache pages, but page boundaries are incidental to sequence order; as a result, attention mass is fragmented across many pages. We propose AttnPack, a learned KV cache layout that repacks keys/values into pagelets so that tokens frequently co-attended for real queries are co-located, using normalized-attention statistics and retrieval-time co-access to build a co-attention graph and solve a size-constrained partitioning. Plugged under Quest-style selectors and Sparse RAG’s per-document gating, AttnPack cuts page fan-out so top-K pages cover most saliency, while a tiny recurrent summary (LESS-style) shadows evicted clusters to preserve recoverability. This co-design of paging and layout targets large IO and latency reductions without retraining, and can be maintained incrementally for streaming inputs.

result.text: The paper addresses the inefficiency of sparsely activated models (SAMs) like Mixture-of-Experts, where scaling parameters does not reliably improve performance and gating-based routing may not be the true bottleneck. The key insight is that deterministic, learned routing is not necessary and that forcing diverse experts to behave consistently via mutual supervision can make randomly activated experts both robust and parameter-efficient. The authors propose THOR, which stochastically activates a random expert per input during training and inference and trains experts with a consistency-regularized loss so each expert learns from ground-truth labels and from other experts as teachers, encouraging aligned predictions across experts. Evaluated on machine translation (including multilingual settings), THOR outperforms standard Transformers and MoE baselines (e.g., +2 BLEU over Switch Transformer) and matches much larger MoE models while using far fewer parameters.

result.text: Epistemic OT-gated specialist curriculum for RL: couple uncertainty-aware MoE routing with an optimal-transport curriculum that progressively moves the training context distribution along Wasserstein geodesics toward high-disagreement regime centers discovered by an ensemble (epistemic POMDP). Train a soft MoE policy/value whose router temperature is modulated by predictive disagreement and whose experts are diversity-regularized via orthogonalization; when persistent regime clusters appear, spawn specialists initialized from the MoE subspace, train them on the corresponding curriculum stages, and distill their behavior back into the MoE to prevent the generalist plateau. The curriculum is recomputed online as beliefs shift, and in nonstationary streams a GP-style mixture dynamics model triggers change-point updates and specialist reactivation. This unifies curriculum shaping, uncertainty-conditioned routing, and generalist–specialist transfer to improve zero-shot generalization and sample efficiency on procedurally diverse and drifting benchmarks.

result.text: We propose Conformal-Constrained Test-Time Adaptation (CoCo-TTA), an online wrapper that couples entropy-minimization with an explicit calibration-control constraint to maintain long-run coverage while improving accuracy under shift. A streaming conformal monitor tracks nonconformity quantiles on a small reservoir and updates a dual variable that jointly scales the adaptation step size and a trust-region penalty; updates are triggered by a martingale shift detector and applied only to low-entropy, diverse samples. The resulting primal–dual procedure minimizes marginal-entropy (or pseudo-label loss) subject to matching a target coverage/calibration profile, with rollback if reservoir coverage or an entropy–sharpness surrogate degrades. CoCo-TTA yields safe, selective adaptation that boosts accuracy under shift while preserving near-nominal calibration in the no-shift regime.

result.text: We propose Structured Scene-Graph Energy Decoding (SSED), a training-free controller that steers LVLM generation with a global scene-level objective. At each step, SSED builds a provisional text scene graph from the partial output and scores it against a visual graph composed from open-vocabulary detectors and HOI predictors using an energy that (i) penalizes unsupported nodes/relations, (ii) rewards coverage of high-confidence objects with a budgeted, non-duplicative set term, and (iii) enforces mutual consistency among triplets. This energy augments HALC-style local grounding with global beam re-ranking, suppressing spurious objects and predicates while preserving fluency; we expect measurable gains on multi-object benchmarks like ROPE and relation-focused suites. SSED unifies ideas from detector-guided grounding and post-hoc rescoring into a single decoding-time structure, requiring no retraining.

result.text: We propose LA-KV: a learning-augmented, robust KV paging layer for long-context LLMs. A tiny predictor emits a one-bit hint per cache page at each step—"reuse within the next phase" vs. "safe to evict"—computed from normalized-attention surrogates (ZipCache-style) and recent query statistics; a Quest-like selector then loads only the hinted top-K while Ada-KV assigns per-head budgets. We import one-bit paging theory to craft an eviction/selection rule that is consistent under perfect hints yet preserves competitive worst-case guarantees under adversarial hints, and we add a small recurrent summary (LESS) so mistaken evictions remain recoverable. This yields query-aware, theoretically grounded paging that cuts IO and latency without sacrificing long-range recall.

Its key insight is that user-provided advice—formalized as potentially partial, fragmented, or imperfect deterministic finite automata (DFAs)—can be incorporated to guide learning and speed up discovery of the hidden reward structure without requiring the reward function to be fully specified. result.text: We propose focus/aperture-coded interventions for object-centric multi-view causal representation under occlusion: vary per-view focus distance and f-number (or sweep focus during exposure) so that depth-dependent defocus toggles which slots are sharp versus blurred, producing unlabeled, slot-targeted appearance changes. Under compositional irreducibility and smooth view-dependent mixing, identifiability holds when the view-by-episode focus schedule induces a pairwise-connected co-visibility-with-sharpness graph and a RIP/expander-like code over depth-ordered slots; a differentiable optics layer models circle-of-confusion PSFs to align slots across focus states. We instantiate a planner that co-designs camera poses and focus/aperture sequences to maximize these identifiability metrics given coarse depth priors, and a slot-contrastive encoder with defocus-aware gating and cycle/anchor losses, achieving fewer episodes than lighting/object perturbations while remaining robust to heavy occlusions. This complements illumination- and occluder-coded designs and turns camera-internal optics into actionable, low-cost interventions.

result.text: We propose a conservative contextual bandit controller for test-time adaptation that selects, per-batch, among a toolkit of lightweight primitives (e.g., TTN-style moment interpolation, sharpness-aware entropy minimization, and forward-only prompt/activation shifts) using context features like uncertainty, augmentation consistency, OOD scores, and class-imbalance indicators. The controller optimizes an unsupervised surrogate reward that blends entropy reduction with stability/sharpness penalties and agreement on a small class-balanced replay reservoir to counter non-i.i.d. streams, while enforcing a safety constraint that rejects actions predicted to harm an in-distribution memory buffer, yielding online regret-style guarantees. This compute-aware policy learns when to adapt, how aggressively, and with which primitive under mixed, noisy shifts, outperforming fixed-method baselines and avoiding collapse. The approach is plug-and-play, wrapping existing TTA modules and learning the scheduling policy online without labels.

result.text: We propose CoR-TTA, a conformal-guarded wrapper that turns any test-time adaptation (TTA) step into a sequential accept/reject decision with long-run error control. It builds unlabeled conformity scores from augmentation-marginal entropy and consistency, monitors their stream with a betting-martingale to detect shift, and maintains an online conformal acceptance band; a candidate parameter update is accepted only if it reduces the held-out reservoir’s conformal risk proxy, otherwise it is rolled back. Updates operate on reliability-filtered, low-entropy, diverse samples and use lightweight, Fisher-regularized (or parameter-efficient) changes to preserve in-distribution performance. By unifying change detection, reliability-aware selection, and online conformal calibration, CoR-TTA adapts when needed while provably limiting false adaptations and preserving calibration when no shift occurs.

result.text: The paper addresses why reinforcement learning agents often fail to generalize from limited training environments to unseen test conditions, arguing that the sequential decision-making setting creates a distinct challenge not captured by supervised-learning generalization analysis. The key insight is that uncertainty about which training conditions will occur at test time induces implicit partial observability—turning nominally fully observed MDPs into “epistemic POMDPs” whose hidden state encodes epistemic uncertainty about environment parameters. The authors formalize this epistemic POMDP and show that methods ignoring the induced partial observability fail, then propose a simple ensemble-based approach that approximates inference over the hidden epistemic state and thereby better conditions policies on uncertainty. Empirically, their ensemble-derived method significantly improves generalization on Procgen compared to baselines, supporting the view that RL generalization requires explicitly addressing epistemic partial observability.

result.text: We propose CoTTA-C: a conformal-triggered, safe test-time adaptation wrapper that maintains online prediction-set coverage certificates and triggers updates only when coverage or a martingale-detected shift in entropy-based nonconformity departs from the source regime. Upon trigger, CoTTA-C routes adaptation along one of two paths: label-prior recalibration using no-label online label-shift estimators, or covariate adaptation using high-confidence, class-uniform filtering with sharpness-aware entropy minimization under a Fisher trust region. Each micro-update is validated on a small reservoir by checking recovery of target coverage and the nonconformity distribution; failing updates are rolled back to prevent collapse. This yields robust, calibrated TTA that adapts only when necessary and disentangles label vs. covariate shift while remaining efficient.

The key insight is that prompt-level KV-state sharing can be maximized across a distributed serving fleet if scheduling jointly optimizes reuse of precomputed KV states and balances computational load, rather than treating reuse and load balancing independently. The authors design Preble, a distributed scheduling system that implements a new scheduling algorithm and a hierarchical scheduler to decide where to cache and reuse KV states and how to route and place inference work across GPUs to exploit shared prompt structure. Evaluated on real workloads and open-source LLMs, Preble yields substantial reductions in average and p99 latency compared to state-of-the-art serving systems.

result.text: We propose Counterfactual Temporal Monitors: causal-LTL reward checkers that operate in a world model’s latent structural causal model to make satisfaction robust to spurious correlations. We align natural-language specs to LTL and compile them into automata whose atomic propositions are evaluated not only on predicted latents but also on counterfactual rollouts under targeted interventions that break nuisance factors, yielding invariant lower/upper satisfaction bounds that the policy maximizes during imagination. Conformal uncertainty from latent proposition classifiers is combined with intervention sets to control risk, and an active loop triggers data collection or queries to privileged “restraining bolt” features when counterfactual disagreement exceeds a budget. Discrete latent branching handles stochastic/partially observed dynamics, while aligning vision/language to the generative latent space mitigates modality gaps—building directly on latent-space monitors like ULTRA/CoForm.

args.text: We propose polarization-coded interventions for object-centric multi-view causal representation under occlusion: rotate linear polarizers on illuminants and sensors to induce per-slot, angle-dependent specular/diffuse contrasts that act as unlabeled, slot-targeted perturbations even when objects overlap in the image. Under a dichromatic BRDF with generic normals/materials, identifiability follows when the angle-by-view-by-episode schedule yields a pairwise-connected co-visibility-with-polarization graph and a RIP/expander-like code over slots in Stokes space; cross-angle specular peaks provide change anchors that align slots across views. We instantiate a planner that co-designs camera poses and polarization sweeps by maximizing a submodular surrogate that reduces code coherence, and a slot-contrastive encoder with a differentiable polarization rendering head that estimates per-slot Stokes parameters and uses group-sparse angle-difference penalties to localize which slot changed. Compared to direction-only lighting or object perturbations, polarization coding is low-power, calibration-light, robust to shadows/glare, and achieves comparable identifiability with fewer episodes.

result.text: The paper tackles the challenge that unlike supervised learning, reinforcement learning (RL) often fails to benefit from larger model parameter counts and can even degrade as size increases. Its key insight is that Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), especially soft MoE routing, can unlock meaningful parameter scaling in value-based RL by sparsely activating specialized expert sub-networks so the overall capacity grows without overwhelming training or causing destructive interference. The authors integrate Soft MoE modules into value networks and empirically evaluate across multiple training regimes and model sizes, showing consistent performance improvements and enabling larger models to improve rather than deteriorate, thereby providing strong evidence toward establishing scaling laws for RL.

result.text: The paper addresses instability of online test-time adaptation (TTA) under realistic “wild” test conditions—mixed distribution shifts, small batches, and online class imbalance—where adapting a pretrained model can fail or collapse to trivial solutions. The key insight is that normalization layers strongly influence TTA stability (batch norm harms while group/layer norm help) but failures persist because a few noisy test samples with large gradients can drive the model into sharp minima that collapse predictions. The authors propose SAR, a sharpness-aware and reliable entropy-minimization method that first filters or downweights high-gradient noisy samples and then optimizes for flat minima to make the adapted model robust to remaining noise; empirically SAR stabilizes adaptation across challenging scenarios while remaining computationally efficient.

result.text: Contingency-Aware Planning (CAP) builds fallback-aware execution graphs for LLM tool agents, selecting both primary and contingency toolchains to bound tail risk and budget overruns. It learns calibrated per-step failure and latency distributions by fusing emulator-simulated outcomes with on-policy traces, then solves a constrained stochastic planning problem to allocate minimal-cost k-alternative branches and trigger policies. At runtime, before high-risk or ambiguous invocations, CAP injects contrastive, tool-specific clarifications and enables rapid intra-toolkit substitution when early anomaly signals fire. Evaluated with stepwise progress and failure-severity metrics on realistic tool tasks, CAP aims to reduce catastrophic dead-ends with modest overhead while producing actionable diagnostics for tool designers.

result.text: The paper addresses hallucinations in large vision-language models (LVLMs), where generated text can diverge from image content, noting that existing visual contrastive decoding methods fail to reliably suppress hallucinatory tokens due to uncontrolled global visual uncertainty. The key insight is that contrastive decoding’s effectiveness depends on precisely amplifying the preference gap between hallucinated and target tokens, which can be achieved by replacing noisy global uncertainty signals with a learned, theoretically grounded preference model to more accurately identify and penalize hallucinatory outputs. The authors propose Hallucination-Induced Optimization (HIO), which fine-tunes a Contrary Bradley-Terry preference model to amplify contrasts between hallucinatory and correct tokens and then uses this model to guide contrastive decoding, thereby more effectively discouraging hallucinations. Experiments across multiple benchmarks show HIO reduces hallucinations and outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of slow inference for long-context large language models, where self-attention becomes bottlenecked by loading a large key-value (KV) cache as sequence length grows. The key insight is that only a small subset of KV cache tokens are critical for a particular query and that token criticality depends on the query vector, so one can predict which cache pages matter without scanning the whole cache. They propose Quest, a query-aware KV cache page selection algorithm that maintains min/max key summaries per cache page and uses the query to estimate page criticality, loading only the top-K pages for attention; this approach yields large self-attention and end-to-end latency speedups (up to 2.23x and 7.03x respectively) with negligible accuracy loss on long-dependency tasks.

result.text: We propose Retrieval-Amortized Test-Time Adaptation (RATTA): instead of performing per-neighbor gradient updates at inference, a small hypernetwork maps a query plus its retrieved examples to per-layer low‑rank adapter weights and an instance‑specific early‑exit policy, enabling fast, gradient‑free conditioning. The hypernetwork is trained to distill the effect of gradient-based test-time training on retrieved neighbors, while also learning to route or compose from a library of reusable adapters for further efficiency. At inference, the frozen base LM is modulated by the generated adapters, and a patience-calibrated exit head halts computation on easy inputs, preserving most of the gains of retrieval TTT at a fraction of the latency. This combines the accuracy benefits of retrieval-driven adaptation with amortized modulation and adapter reuse to yield scalable, compute‑aware online adaptation.

result.text: The paper tackles how to train deep RL agents to follow a wide range of temporally extended, compositional instructions written in linear temporal logic (LTL) so they can generalize to new tasks in multi-task environments. The key insight is to leverage LTL’s compositional syntax and formal semantics to structure learning so that a policy can be conditioned on LTL formulas and thereby recombine learned sub-behaviors to satisfy unseen instructions. The method trains task-conditioned policies using representations that align with LTL structure and semantics, augmented by an environment-agnostic LTL pretraining scheme that teaches the agent LTL semantics once to improve sample efficiency downstream. Empirical results on discrete and continuous domains with combinatorially large task sets show the approach generalizes to and successfully solves many unseen LTL-specified tasks.
